subject: systems
title: The idle board
one_line: Six coprime cadences, an absence credited in full, and a total you are not allowed to maximise.

sections.heading: Why the periods are prime
body: Six longhouses tick on periods 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 and 13. If two of them shared a factor they would fire together forever after, and the board would walk one diagonal of its state space instead of the whole lattice.

Coprime is the whole requirement, and it has a consequence you can compute: the pattern of which halls fire together repeats after the least common multiple of the periods, and for pairwise coprime numbers the lcm IS the product. Thirty thousand and thirty ticks. Change one period to four and it collapses — 4 and 2 share a factor, and the answer stops being the product.
This is worth writing yourself rather than reading, because the lcm is the difference between a board that surprises you for a day and one that repeats before lunch.

sections.heading: The absence is credited in full
body: The board keeps a timestamp of when it last saw you. On load it works out how many ticks it missed and runs every one of them. There is no cap, no decay, and no bonus for having been present.

That last part is the design decision and it is not generosity. The moment presence is rewarded, the optimal play is to sit there, and an idle game whose optimal play is to sit there has become a job with a progress bar. Crediting the absence exactly is what keeps it from turning into one.

sections.heading: You cannot maximise the total
body: Pressing a button on that board never raises output. It chooses which clan receives the next house — the composition — and nothing else. Total production is a function of time and tier, and tier only ever rises.

A game whose output can be maximised is a game that can be played wrong, and a game that can be played wrong has somebody in it who is behind. There is nobody behind on that board. What you can be is differently composed, and the deck has a composition it actually wants, so the interesting question is distance from it rather than size of it.

Distance is allowed to move in both directions. The RECORD of the closest you ever came is not. That split — a live figure that may fall beside a record that may not — is the whole of the +1 law expressed in two variables, and the audit you are about to write checks it.

sections.heading: What an audit is for
body: The board saves its whole state under one key in this browser. You are going to read it and check three things: that it has actually run, that its record has never fallen behind its current figure, and that nothing in it records a loss.

The third is the one worth dwelling on. You are not checking that no loss occurred. You are checking that the data structure has no place to put one — which is a stronger statement, and the only kind of guarantee a schema can give you.

practice.brief: Write lcm, perTick, firesOn and audit. The first three are marked against fixtures. audit is marked against fixtures too, and then readBoard is checked against your actual saved board. Type check.

checks.name: six coprime cadences realign after their product
and sharing a factor collapses it
lcm of one number is that number
the board at tier one puts out the sum of yield over period
tick 6 fires the twos and the threes and nothing else
tick 30030 fires every one of them
an audit of a board that has run says so
an audit of an untouched board says it has not
a record behind the live figure is caught
checks.test: audit({t: 9, bestFit: 40, fitNow: 55, stock:{}}).recordHolds === false && audit({t: 9, bestFit: 71, fitNow: 55, stock:{}}).recordHolds === true

checks.name: a state with a place to record a loss is caught
checks.test: audit({t: 9, bestFit: 1, fitNow: 1, stock:{}, casualties: 0}).lossFree === false && audit({t: 9, bestFit: 1, fitNow: 1, stock:{}}).lossFree === true

checks.name: readBoard goes to the board’s own key and nowhere else
and invents nothing when the key is empty
checks.test: (() => { const real = localStorage.getItem('venus.clans.v1'); try { localStorage.removeItem('venus.clans.v1'); return readBoard() === null; } finally { if (real !== null) localStorage.setItem('venus.clans.v1', real); } })()

ask: Run your audit on your own board. If recordHolds is ever false, one of us has a bug and it is worth finding out which.
